meta.title: Tantric Prayer
meta.subtitle: Thirty-Six Prayers for the Inner Weather
meta.blurb: the nine rasas · four prayers each · kashmir shaivism
meta.epi_iast: api labdhabhavadbhāvaḥ svātmollāsamayaṃ jagat / paśyan bhaktirasābhogair bhaveyam aviyojitaḥ
meta.epi_en: seeing the world as the delight of the self — may i never be parted from it, through the enjoyment of devotion's rasa.

entries.title: The Un-Drunk One's Thirst
entries.en:
may the higher knowledge come from tasting the nectar of your devotion —
that state, lord, turn toward me,
keen as the not-yet-drunk one's thirst for the first drink.
entries.brief: Desire as holy thirst — rati aimed at God instead of at the world.
entries.logic: The sthāyin rati is not to be removed but redirected. The verse names the exact texture: nāsavas-śuktatā, the eagerness of one who has NOT yet tasted — the pre-taste longing. Knowledge itself (bodha) comes by the sip; the prayer is therefore for the thirst to be aimed at him, and for the state to turn toward the speaker.
entries.howto: When longing is loud: say the verse and let the object of the longing become the taste of devotion rather than the thing you'd grab. Feeling-tip: keep the ache — it is the rasa before it arrives; the thirst IS the practice.
entries.iast: bhavadbhaktyamṛtāsvādād bodhasya syāt parāpi yā / daśā sā māṃ prati svāmin nāsavasyeva śuktatā
entries.devanagari: भवद्भक्त्यमृतास्वादाद् बोधस्य स्यात् परापि या / दशा सा मां प्रति स्वामिन् नासवस्येव शुक्तता

entries.title: The Wine of Non-Difference
entries.en:
let me not spend one moment here as anything
other than your servant's vessel — one who reverently,
unceasingly drinks the rasa-wine of your non-difference.
entries.brief: Devotion as intoxication: the wine is non-duality itself.
entries.logic: Abheda-rasāsava — the wine of non-difference. Śṛṅgāra's whole lexicon (wine, tasting, the beloved's feet) is applied to the doctrine: the beloved is not other, and the intoxication is the insight. The sthāyin rati becomes the taste of the one, and the servant becomes the vessel that holds it.
entries.howto: When you crave closeness to something: say it and re-cast — the wine is already poured (non-difference); you are the cup. Feeling-tip: warmth as if from a sip; the distance you wanted to close was the fiction.
entries.iast: kṣaṇam apīha na tāvakadāsatāṃ prati bhaveyam ahaṃ kila bhājanam / bhavadabhedarasāsavam ādarād avirataṃ rasayeyam ahaṃ na cet
entries.devanagari: क्षणम् अपीह न तावकदासतां प्रति भवेयम् अहं किल भाजनम् / भवदभेदरसासवम् आदराद् अविरतं रसयेयम् अहं न चेत्

entries.title: What Delight, Beloved
entries.iast: ambudaiḥ śikhigaṇo vinādyate kā ratiḥ priya mayā vinādya te
entries.en:
by clouds the peacock-flock is sounded —
what delight, beloved, without me today?
entries.brief: Love-in-separation given to the whole landscape — the peacock's cry.
entries.logic: Ghatakarpara, Kṣemarāja's night of the broken pot, frames longing as weather: the peacocks cry at cloud-arrival — and the cry is 'without me.' Vipralambha (longing-in-separation) is outsourced to the scene until the self-pity becomes a rainstorm that belongs to everyone. The ache is seasonal, not personal.
entries.howto: When longing for someone or something: say it as the peacock line — the cry is appropriate, beautiful, and will end with the rain. Feel the ache as weather: you are the bird, not the drowning.
entries.devanagari: अम्बुदैः शिखिगणो विनाद्यते का रतिः प्रिय मया विनाद्य ते

entries.title: The Moon That Carries the Nectar
entries.en:
give me one glance of yours — light, cool, pure,
like the moon's crescent, carrying nectar —
o lord, for my desire itself.
entries.brief: The cool moon-glance that carries desire instead of burning it.
entries.logic: Kāma (desire) is not banned here but delivered amṛta: the verse asks for a dṛś, a gaze that is śītalā (cool) like the moon's crescent and amṛta-vāhinī (nectar-bearing). The erotic voltage of rati is converted into moonlight — desire needs cooling and nourishment, not cutting.
entries.howto: When desire runs hot: one breath in, offer the heat upward as the thing that needs the glance, and picture the crescent-cool gaze landing on it. The prayer cools by image, not by prohibition. Feeling-tip: the heat stays but stops being an emergency.
entries.iast: prakāśāṃ śītalām ekāṃ śuddhāṃ śaśikalām iva / dṛśaṃ vitara me nātha kām apy amṛtavāhinīm
entries.devanagari: प्रकाशां शीतलाम् एकां शुद्धां शशिकलाम् इव / दृशं वितर मे नाथ काम् अप्य् अमृतवाहिनीम्

entries.title: Laughing, Dancing, Eating It All
entries.en:
where he laughs and dances, where desire and hatred themselves are eaten,
where the nectar-rasa of devotion is drunk —
may i attain that state.
entries.brief: The state where he laughs, dances, and eats the klesas for lunch.
entries.logic: Hāsa's sthāyin hāsa is made cosmic: the divine one laughs and dances, and — the key verb — rāga-dveṣe bhujyate, desire and hatred are CONSUMED as food. Mirth here is not humour; it is the sound of digestion. The negative emotions are not banished from the state; they are the meal.
entries.howto: Say it when something finally stops being infuriating — and notice the laugh that arrives is the verse working. Feeling-tip: the annoyance is suddenly chewable; that is bhujyate happening. Let the laugh be the proof.
entries.iast: hasyate nṛtyate yatra rāgadveṣādi bhujyate / pīyate bhaktipīyūṣarasas tat prāpnuyāṃ padam
entries.devanagari: हस्यते नृत्यते यत्र रागद्वेषादि भुज्यते / पीयते भक्तिपीयूषरसस् तत् प्राप्नुयां पदम्

entries.title: The Essence of Laughter
entries.en:
in this three-world joke whose essence is laughter —
to you alone, the non-dual, the one seated in eternal joy:
namas.
entries.brief: Bowing to the Lord who sits on laughter itself.
entries.logic: The universe is upahāsa-ekasāra — the essence of the cosmic joke — and the Lord is nitya-sukha-āsina, seated in eternal joy. Laughter is not irreverence but the metaphysical register of the world-as-play seen from inside. You bow TO the seated laughter rather than laughing at him: reverence and joke in one breath.
entries.howto: When life turns absurd: say it, and read the absurdity as his seat. Feeling-tip: irreverence without disrespect — the sigh turns into a chuckle, and the chuckle lands on him.
entries.iast: upahāsaikasāre 'sminn etāvati jagattraye / tubhyam evādvitīyāya namo nityasukhāsine
entries.devanagari: उपहासैकसारे ऽस्मिन्न् एतावति जगत्त्रये / तुभ्यम् एवाद्वितीयाय नमो नित्यसुखासिने

entries.title: His Laughing-Play
entries.en:
victorious are your servants, lord of the worlds —
for whom this ocean of saṃsāra
is a laughing-play.
entries.brief: Same ocean as everyone else's; for his servants it's a playground.
entries.logic: Everyone else drowns in saṃsārārṇava — the ocean of becoming. For yeṣāṃ (for those servants) it is krīḍā-hāsara: a park of laughter and play. Hāsa changes the ownership of the ocean, not its water. The rasa-shift happens before the circumstance shifts — the ocean is the fact, the playground is the flavour.
entries.howto: In a hard moment, name it: ocean. Then say the verse, and the water becomes shallow. Feeling-tip: the shoulders drop and the mouth lifts before the situation changes at all.
entries.iast: jayanti te jagadvandyā dāsās te jagatāṃ vibho / saṃsārārṇava evaiṣa yeṣāṃ krīḍāmahāsaraḥ
entries.devanagari: जयन्ति ते जगद्वन्द्या दासास् ते जगतां विभो / संसारार्णव एवैष येषां क्रीडामहासरः

entries.title: Angry, Then Laughing, Then Śiva
entries.brief: The permission slip: devotion lets you rage, then laugh, then shout.
entries.logic: The verse gives the full emotional sequence and blesses every step: bhakti-kṣīva (drunk on devotion) → kupyeyam (let me be angry!) → haseyaṃ (then laugh) → udyām (rise) → raṭeyam śivety (shout Śiva). Anger is not the failure of the practice but its middle passage — it converts to laughter to shout. Hāsa is the hinge where the negative becomes praise.
entries.howto: When worked up: say it as an instruction manual — drunk first, then let it become laugh, rise, and shout. The last word must be Śiva, out loud if you dare. Feeling-tip: the anger doesn't get suppressed; it gets promoted.
entries.iast: bhaktikṣīvo 'pi kupyeyaṃ bhavāyānuśayīya ca / tathā haseyaṃ udyāṃ ca raṭeyaṃ ca śivety alam
entries.devanagari: भक्तिक्षीवो ऽपि कुप्येयं भवायानुशयीय च / तथा हसेयं उद्यां च रटेयं च शिवेत्य् अलम्

entries.title: The Seed of Sorrow
entries.en:
strange, lord: this mind is by nature the seed of sorrow —
yet watered with the rasa of your devotion
it ripens into the highest fruit.
entries.brief: The sorrow-seed that ripens instead of rotting.
entries.logic: The verse concedes the grief outright: manaḥ is duḥkha-bīja by nature (nisargataḥ) — the mind was born a grief-seed. The surprise (citra!) is the alchemy: watered with bhakti-rasa it becomes niḥśreyasa-mahāphala, the highest fruit. Karuṇā is not healed by removal but by irrigation — the same seed, different harvest.
entries.howto: In grief: say it and water the seed instead of cursing the soil. Feeling-tip: the grief stays, but it is being used; even the tears count as irrigation.
entries.iast: citraṃ nisargato nātha duḥkhabījam idaṃ manaḥ / tvadbhaktirasasaṃsiktam niḥśreyasamahāphalam
entries.devanagari: चित्रं निसर्गतो नाथ दुःखबीजम् इदं मनः / त्वद्भक्तिरससंसिक्तम् निःश्रेयसमहाफलम्

entries.title: The Flood Over Joy and Sorrow
entries.en:
the flood of nectar from meditating you overflows
joy and sorrow alike — like waters filling
all the low and lower lands.
entries.brief: One flood levels the hierarchy of gladness and grief.
entries.logic: A single amṛta-pūra (flood of nectar from dhyāna) covers harṣa AND śoka samam — equally, like water filling every lowland. Sorrow gets no special treatment and no special exclusion: both emotions are terrain, and the flood is the same. Karuṇā's transformation is levelling, not fixing.
entries.howto: Say it in either state — grief or glee — the verse works on the level of the field, not the feeling. Feeling-tip: a settling, as if water found its level; the ranking of emotions collapses.
entries.iast: harṣāṇām atha śokānāṃ sarveṣāṃ plāvakaḥ samam / bhavaddhyānāmṛtāpūro nimnāṇimnabhuvām iva
entries.devanagari: हर्षाणाम् अथ शोकानां सर्वेषां प्लावकः समम् / भवद्ध्यानामृतापूरो निम्नाणिम्नभुवाम् इव

entries.title: Sorrow Mixed with Ghee
entries.en:
lord, the countless sorrows even of the world-dweller —
mixed with your own self they become ghee:
they come to be bearable.
entries.brief: Sorrow mixed with Śiva-self becomes ghee — and ghee is bearable.
entries.logic: The alchemical verse: duḥkha + bhavat-īya-ātman (your own self) = ghṛta (ghee). Ghee does not remove the ingredient — it transforms its texture: the sharp is suspended in the smooth. The grief survives as substance but not as edge. Karuṇā's medicine is texture change, not argument.
entries.howto: In pain: say the ghee line and literally imagine the sharp edge of the feeling being coated. Feeling-tip: the body responds to texture, not to reasons — the tightness loosens because the sharpness is now suspended.
entries.iast: deva duḥkhāny aśeṣāṇi yāni saṃsāriṇām api / ghṛtyākhyabhavadīyātmayutāny āyānti sahyatām
entries.devanagari: देव दुःखान्य् अशेषाणि यानि संसारिणाम् अपि / घृत्याख्यभवदीयात्मयुतान्य् आयान्ति सह्यताम्

entries.title: The Banner Against Suffering
entries.en:
o lord, the banner that destroys the suffering of the bowing —
treasure of good, dhūrjaṭa: for me whose only home is sorrow,
afraid of birth and death — so act for me, that while yet living
i may enjoy the sweet taste of the good sense-objects,
unshakeable, the powers in service of your worship.
entries.brief: The emergency prayer: grief addressed to the Destroyer-of-pain by name.
entries.logic: The Lord is named by function: praṇatārti-nāśana-paṭa — the flag that annihilates the pain of the one who bows. The verse locates the speaker without self-pity: ālaya-eka — sorrow is the only house I know, and I fear birth and death. The grief is fully stated before the name is invoked — confession first, then the banner.
entries.howto: At 3am in the pit: say the whole confession first, then the name. Feeling-tip: the banner is real — a flag planted IN the grief, not flying over it. The fear of birth and death can be said out loud; that's the verse's permission.
entries.iast: he nātha praṇatārtināśanapaṭo śreyonidhe dhūrjaṭe duḥkhaikāyatanasya janmamaraṇatrastasya me sāmpratam / tac ceṣṭasva yathā manojñaviṣayāsvādapradā uttamā jīvann eva samaśnuve 'ham acalāḥ siddhīs tvadarcāparaḥ
entries.devanagari: हे नाथ प्रणतार्तिनाशनपटो श्रेयोनिधे धूर्जटे दुःखैकायतनस्य जन्ममरणत्रस्तस्य मे साम्प्रतम् / तच् चेष्टस्व यथा मनोज्ञविषयास्वादप्रदा उत्तमा जीवन्न् एव समश्नुवे ऽहम् अचलाः सिद्धीस् त्वदर्चापरः

entries.title: The Axe of 'All Is His'
entries.en:
'this is mine, this is not yours' — the roots of attachment and aversion, hard-shackled;
o lord, let the axe of the one conviction 'all is your-become' fall on them in me.
entries.brief: The engine of rage is mine-ness; the axe is the conviction that all is his.
entries.logic: Anger's roots are rāga-dveṣa driven by mamaka (mine-ness) — 'etan mama, na tv idam' (this is mine, this is not yours). The remedy named is an instrument: paraśu, the axe of ekatva-pratyaya — the conviction that everything is bhavanmaya, his-become. The verse PRAYS FOR THE AXE TO FALL — an act, not a mood.
entries.howto: In rage: name the possession first — 'mine', 'not yours' — then say the verse at it. Feeling-tip: the fist unclenches not by relaxing but by losing the ownership record; the thing remains, the claiming ends.
entries.iast: etan mama na tv idam iti rāgadveṣādinigaḍadṛḍhamūle / nātha bhavanmayataikyapratyayaparaśuḥ patatvantaḥ
entries.devanagari: एतन् मम न त्व् इदम् इति रागद्वेषादिनिगडदृढमूले / नाथ भवन्मयतैक्यप्रत्ययपरशुः पतत्वन्तः

entries.title: Let the Anger Ripen
entries.en:
the mind purified by the complete ripening of
honour and dishonour, rāga and the rest —
such a devotee: how could he have ordinary-world conduct?
entries.brief: Pride, slight and rage treated as things that must fully ripen first.
entries.logic: Māna, avamāna (honour and dishonour), rāga — these must NIṢPĀKA, ripen completely, like poison cooked out or fruit brought to sweetness. The purified mind is the one where the indignation-mix has finished its fermentation. The verse reframes the anger-process itself: give it heat and time, and the result is clarity instead of explosion.
entries.howto: When slighted: say it and let the feeling ripen rather than react — the insult is being cooked, not served. Feeling-tip: the heat continues but stops being an instruction to act.
entries.iast: mānāvamānarāgādiniṣpākavimalaṃ manaḥ / yasyāsau bhaktimāṃl lokatulyaśīlaḥ kathaṃ bhavet
entries.devanagari: मानावमानरागादिनिष्पाकविमलं मनः / यस्यासौ भक्तिमांल् लोकतुल्यशीलः कथं भवेत्

entries.title: Devotion Conquers the Darkness
entries.en:
in whose case even the darkness of attachment and aversion
has been conquered by the brilliance of devotion —
what to speak of the learned, among such exalted ones?
entries.brief: Rage is a lightless state; devotion is the light that ends it.
entries.logic: Rāga-dveṣa are andhakāra — darkness; bhakti-tviṣ, the brilliance of devotion, is the conqueror. The verse gives light-physics to anger: not fight the dark, but shine. And what remains after conquest is not the repressed but mahīyas — the exalted, lit-up ones. The learned don't even rate in comparison.
entries.howto: Say it as a light-switch claim: the anger is dark, and you are switching on devotion rather than wrestling the dark. Feeling-tip: warmth precedes relief — that order is the physics.
entries.iast: rāgadveṣandhakāro 'pi yeṣāṃ bhaktitviṣā jitaḥ / teṣāṃ mahīyasām agre katame jñānaśālinaḥ
entries.devanagari: रागद्वेषन्धकारो ऽपि येषां भक्तित्विषा जितः / तेषां महीयसाम् अग्रे कतमे ज्ञानशालिनः

entries.title: Your Wrath Purifies
entries.en:
also worthy of praise, O supreme, are those
made pure by the touch of your wrath's fire
even when you have destroyed them.
entries.brief: Even his wrath is a purifier — so the fire itself is praised.
entries.logic: Tvat-kopa-pāvaka — the fire of your wrath — is pāvaka, a purifier, by definition. Those touched (even annihilated) by it are pūtā, purified. Raudra's rasa seen from the other side: divine anger is cauterisation, not punishment. The devotee's praise of THAT is the final surrender of the complaint against anger itself.
entries.howto: When caught in a rage — yours or someone's's: say it, and re-classify the fire as purifying touch before responding. Feeling-tip: the flinch converts to a bow.
entries.iast: vandyās te 'pi mahīyāṃsaḥ pralayopagatā api / tvatkopapāvakasparśapūtā ye parameśvara
entries.devanagari: वन्द्यास् ते ऽपि महीयांसः प्रलयोपगता अपि / त्वत्कोपपावकस्पर्शपूता ये परमेश्वर

entries.title: Victory — the World Depends on Him
entries.en:
victory, lord — namas, namas to you:
this entire universe depends on you;
you are the supreme lord of the worlds, the one —
in you alone i take refuge.
entries.brief: The victory-cry that puts the whole world on his back.
entries.logic: Vīra's sthāyin utsāha begins with jaya — twice — then the cosmic dependency: sakalaṃ viśvam idaṃ tavāśritam, everything rests on YOU. The hero's strength is deliberately outsourced: your energy becomes his vehicle rather than your own inventory. Enthusiasm as alignment, not as ego.
entries.howto: Morning, before the task: say it once under the breath, fast. Feeling-tip: the chest widens; effort turns from strain into celebration because the weight is his, not yours.
entries.iast: jaya deva namo namo 'stu te sakalaṃ viśvam idaṃ tavāśritam / jagatāṃ parameśvaro bhavān paramekaḥ śaraṇāgato 'smi te
entries.devanagari: जय देव नमो नमो ऽस्तु ते सकलं विश्वम् इदं तवाश्रितम् / जगतां परमेश्वरो भवान् परमेकः शरणागतो ऽस्मि ते

entries.title: May I Become the Grass
entries.en:
when, eyes closed in the tasting of inner devotion-wonder,
i worship 'namas to śiva' —
may i become even the grass [in that place].
entries.brief: So lost in devotion's wonder one would be the grass at the threshold.
entries.logic: The extreme of vīra-bhakti: antar-bhakti-catkāra (inner wonder) savoured until the eyes close (āmīlitekṣaṇa), and the self-offer is to become tṛṇa — grass, trodden, at his doorway. Heroism here is the heroism of disappearance INTO devotion; the glory is to be the least impressive thing present.
entries.howto: When enthusiasm needs depth rather than noise: say it and offer to be the least impressive thing in the room. Feeling-tip: the wanting-to-be-seen dissolves; the energy continues without the vanity.
entries.iast: antarbhakticamatkāracarvaṇāmīlitekṣaṇaḥ / namo mahyaṃ śivāyeti pūjayam syāṃ tṛṇāny api
entries.devanagari: अन्तर्भक्तिचमत्कारचर्वणामीलितेक्षणः / नमो मह्यं शिवायेति पूजयम् स्यां तृणान्य् अपि

entries.title: The Sound That Never Leaves the Mouth
entries.en:
victorious those on whose mouth's circle
the sound of śiva constantly roams —
ever-streaming from the immortal reservoir,
the supreme nectar dripping sweet.
entries.brief: Victory to the constant chanter — japa become involuntary.
entries.logic: Niyataṃ śivadhvaniḥ — the Śiva-sound circulating the face without stop (the gloss: twenty-four hours). Vīra's utsāha here is constancy: practice that has become self-running — the ajapa that the Vijñāna Bhairava describes as breath itself. The verse is a toast to the one whose mantra no longer needs permission.
entries.howto: Say it when you catch the name rising on its own — mid-shower, mid-walk. The verse applauds the practice applauding itself. Feeling-tip: pride WITH devotion; the discipline patting itself on the back.
entries.iast: te jayanti mukhamaṇḍale bhraman asti yeṣu niyataṃ śivadhvaniḥ / yaḥ śāśīva prasṛto 'mṛtāśayāt svādu saṃsravati cāmṛtaṃ param
entries.devanagari: ते जयन्ति मुखमण्डले भ्रमन् अस्ति येषु नियतं शिवध्वनिः / यः शाशीव प्रसृतो ऽमृताशयात् स्वादु संस्रवति चामृतं परम्

entries.title: Praised Because You Worship
entries.en:
o mind, though you are flickering, yet you are praised —
because you worship:
you take refuge in the refuge of the refuges,
the teacher of the three worlds, the beloved of ambikā.
entries.brief: The distracted mind is praised for showing up anyway.
entries.logic: Capala (flickering, unstable) is normally the enemy of every practice — the verse reverses the verdict: slāghyase, you are PRAISED, yato bhajase, because you worship. Utsāha for the distracted: the measure is not steadiness but direction. Even a scattering mind in the direction of refuge earns the praise.
entries.howto: Address it TO your mind, in the second person, when it won't hold — praise it for showing up rather than scolding it for drifting. Feeling-tip: self-compassion as fuel; the scattered mind sits down when praised, not when punished.
entries.iast: capalam asi yad api mānasa tatrāpi ślāghyase yato bhajase / śaraṇānām api śaraṇaṃ tribhuvanagurum ambikākāntam
entries.devanagari: चपलम् असि यद् अपि मानस तत्रापि श्लाघ्यसे यतो भजसे / शरणानाम् अपि शरणं त्रिभुवनगुरुम् अम्बिकाकान्तम्

entries.title: When Will I Suddenly Recognise You
entries.en:
the lord — fearless, generous, full, causeless,
beyond denial of self — when will i suddenly recognise him —
and put the master's own folk to shame?
entries.brief: Addressed to the Lord whose very name is fearlessness.
entries.logic: Bhayānaka's sthāyin bhaya meets Īśvara who is abhaya — fearless — and the cure named is sahasābhijñā, sudden recognition, not calm. The verse's logic: fear is the pre-recognition static, and kadā — when — is a countdown to the flash. Recognising him puts the world (which produced the fear) to shame.
entries.howto: When fear is up: say it as a question, not a plea — kadā? when? Feeling-tip: fear becomes the sound before the recognition rather than the enemy of it. After the last word, expect nothing; the asking is the turning.
entries.iast: īśvaram abhayam udāraṃ pūrṇam akāraṇam apahnutātmānaṃ / sahasābhijñāya kadā svāmijanaṃ lajjayiṣyāmi
entries.devanagari: ईश्वरम् अभयम् उदारं पूर्णम् अकारणम् अपह्नुतात्मानं / सहसाभिज्ञाय कदा स्वामिजनं लज्जयिष्यामि

entries.title: The Full Confession
entries.brief: The full inventory — including the fear of decay — ending in refuge.
entries.logic: The verse itemises the negative self-image without flinching: mūḍha (dull), duḥkhakṛta (sorrow-woven), jarā-doṣa-bhīta (afraid of old age's flaws), śakti-hīna (powerless) — and then the pivot: tavāśritaḥ asmi, I have taken refuge. Named fears lose volume; the inventory ends in a single act of leaning.
entries.howto: List YOUR four in his cadence, then land the last line. Feeling-tip: the inventory leaves the body lighter; the refuge-line is the exhale. Especially for aging-anxiety and inadequacy-shame.
entries.iast: mūḍho 'smi duḥkhakalito 'smi jarādidoṣabhīto 'smi śaktirahito 'smi tavāśrito 'smi / śambho tathā kalaya śīghram upaimi yena sarvottamāṃ dhuram apojjhitaduḥkhamārgaḥ
entries.devanagari: मूढो ऽस्मि दुःखकलितो ऽस्मि जरादिदोषभीतो ऽस्मि शक्तिरहितो ऽस्मि तवाश्रितो ऽस्मि / शम्भो तथा कलय शीघ्रम् उपैमि येन सर्वोत्तमां धुरम् अपोज्झितदुःखमार्गः

entries.title: Between His Feet
entries.en:
residing even between your feet and your devotees' —
i am without fear; in those various planes of being
i would worship the lord, unobstructed in action.
entries.brief: Fearlessness by geography: living in the gap between his feet.
entries.logic: Nivasann antara eva nirbhayaḥ — dwelling in the in-between (between his feet and his people), fearlessness arises not from courage but from LOCATION. The verse gives fear a map: there is a narrow country, foot-adjacent and community-adjacent, where bhaya simply has no border. Fear lives at other addresses.
entries.howto: When fear arrives: find the location instead of fighting the feeling. Imagine the small warm space between his feet; move in. Feeling-tip: the fear stays outside the border like weather reported from another city.
entries.iast: bhavanbhavadīyapādayor nivasann antara eva nirbhayaḥ / bhavabhūmiṣu tāsu tāsv ahaṃ prabhum arceyam anargalakriyaḥ
entries.devanagari: भवन्भवदीयपादयोर् निवसन्न् अन्तर एव निर्भयः / भवभूमिषु तासु तास्व् अहं प्रभुम् अर्चेयम् अनर्गलक्रियः

entries.title: The Scorching Dissolved
entries.en:
when will i come to dwell in the drinking-and-playing
of your devotion-nectar — with the eight powers attained,
and all fear of troubles dissolved?
entries.brief: Anticipatory dread melts in the rasa-cup.
entries.logic: Two claims: the eight siddhis may be attained (the vīra-bait), but the real payload is vigalita-upātāpa-santrāsa — the dread-of-burn having MELTED in the rāsa-drinking. Upātāpa is the scorching anxiety of what's coming; it isn't fought, it is dissolved in the cup. Fear as something you drink through.
entries.howto: Anxious about what's coming? Take the verse as a drink-description and sip your current state as rasa. Feeling-tip: the anticipatory heat cools; the future stops glowing red.
entries.iast: labdhāṇimādisiddhir vigalitasakalopatāpasantrāsaḥ / tvadbhaktirasāyanapānakriḍhāniṣṭaḥ kadāsīya
entries.devanagari: लब्धाणिमादिसिद्धिर् विगलितसकलोपतापसन्त्रासः / त्वद्भक्तिरसायनपानक्रिढानिष्टः कदासीय

entries.title: The Smear That Is Forgetting
entries.en:
even within, the tiniest smear that is my non-contemplation of you —
wiping that, o lord, from everywhere,
[show] your own form.
entries.brief: The impurity isn't filth; it's the lapse of remembering.
entries.logic: The mala is tvad-apratana-kālikā — even the moment's failure to think of him. Bībhatsa's disgust, redirected: the thing that disgusts is not dirt but forgetting. And the wiping (parimṛjya) reveals svarūpa — the cleaner the frame, the more the face shows. Disgust at the stain becomes longing for what the stain hid.
entries.howto: In self-loathing: rename the stain — it is just the lapse of attention. Wipe = return, not scrub. Feeling-tip: the self-hatred loses its subject, and what's left is a fresh look at his form.
entries.iast: antar apy atitarām aṇīyasī yā tvadaprathanakālikāsti me / tām apīśa parimṛjya sarvataḥ svaṃ svarūpam amalaṃ prakāśaya
entries.devanagari: अन्तर् अप्य् अतितराम् अणीयसी या त्वदप्रथनकालिकास्ति मे / ताम् अपीश परिमृज्य सर्वतः स्वं स्वरूपम् अमलं प्रकाशय

entries.title: The Impure Mind, Confessed
entries.en:
in my mind, absolutely impure, my own devotion-vine drowned —
hard: it ripens not even its own,
the unearned blossoms of its fortune.
entries.brief: The raw confession — the devotion-vine drowned in muck.
entries.logic: Bībhatsa at its least polite: maline manasi, the mind is dirty, and the bhakti-latā (devotion-vine) is submerged under it — so even its own virtues don't ripen. Utpaladeva includes the complaint in the hymn-book itself: self-disgust, spoken, IS bhakti's material. The shame is not edited out; it is a verse.
entries.howto: Say it on the days you feel worst about yourself — the hymn says it for you, better. Feeling-tip: honesty displaces shame; the muck, spoken aloud, is at least seen.
entries.iast: manasi maline madīyemagnā tvadbhaktimaṇilatā kaṣṭam / na nijān api tanute tānapauruṣeyān svasampadullāsān
entries.devanagari: मनसि मलिने मदीयेमग्ना त्वद्भक्तिमणिलता कष्टम् / न निजान् अपि तनुते तानपौरुषेयान् स्वसम्पदुल्लासान्

entries.title: The Doubt-Enemy Shattered
entries.en:
the thought-stain in my mind, scoured by the deathless nectar's flood
poured over the trough of refuse — with the invincible doubt-enemy crushed:
let beholding you be unceasing.
entries.brief: The stain's partner in crime is doubt — and seeing breaks both.
entries.logic: The verse names the double-bind: mala (the mind's stain) and the durjaya saṃśaya-vairin (the invincible doubt-enemy). Both are destroyed by ONE thing: tvad-avalokana-janita-phala — the fruit born of beholding him. Disgust's cure is not more scrubbing but darśana, the look. The enemy of clarity was never dirt; it was the un-looked-at.
entries.howto: When the mind feels stained AND doubting: stop scrubbing, start looking — one look inward at the form. Feeling-tip: doubt and disgust fall together because they were both standing in the dark.
entries.iast: kharaniṣedhakhadāmṛtapūraṇocchalitadhautavikalpamalasya me / dalitadurjayasaṃśayavairiṇas tvadavalokanam astu nirantaram
entries.devanagari: खरनिषेधखदामृतपूरणोच्छलितधौतविकल्पमलस्य मे / दलितदुर्जयसंशयवैरिणस् त्वदवलोकनम् अस्तु निरन्तरम्

entries.title: Strike the Dividing-Piece
entries.iast: vilīne śaṅkaughe sapadi paripūrṇe ca vibhave | saṃhārākhyā mama hṛdi bhidāṃśaṃ praharatu
entries.en:
in the melted doubt-heap, at once in full glory —
o lord named dissolution, strike the split portion of my heart.
entries.brief: The hunger that keeps cutting — finished when doubt melts.
entries.logic: Kramastotra's verse from Abhinavagupta's own recitation-list: śaṅkaugha (the doubt-flood) is gone, pūrṇa (fullness) stands — and then ONE request: strike the hṛdi-bhidāṃśa, the fragment that divides the heart. The disgust behind bībhatsa was the partition-making: the inner cutter that keeps fullness in two halves. Saṃhāra (dissolution) finishes the surgery.
entries.howto: After weeks of inner division — this vs that, me vs it: say it as the surgeon's request, once. Feeling-tip: the split seals; the hunger to divide ends with the knife that isn't yours.
entries.devanagari: विलीने शङ्कौघे सपदि परिपूर्णे च विभवे । संहाराख्या मम हृदि भिदांशं प्रहरतु

entries.title: The Wonder of the Word at Tongue-Tip
entries.en:
when the single word śiva stands ever at the tongue's tip —
the taste of all sense-objects exists in the devotee alone.
what a wonder!
entries.brief: One word at tongue-tip transmutes every taste into rasa.
entries.logic: The verse compresses Vijñāna: the mantra at the organ of taste (jihvāgra) transmutes all viṣaya-āsvāda — every sense-object is tasted as devotion. The aho! is technical: it is vismaya at the mechanism itself — wonder as the experience of the doctrine working. Adbhuta is testable in one bite.
entries.howto: When anything tastes or sounds flat: place Śiva at the tongue's tip and re-taste the next sip or bite. Feeling-tip: the wonder is measurable — if the flavour deepens, the verse is real.
entries.iast: śiva ity ekaśabdasya jihvāgre tiṣṭhataḥ sadā / samastaviṣayāsvādo bhakteṣv evāsti ko 'py aho
entries.devanagari: शिव इत्य् एकशब्दस्य जिह्वाग्रे तिष्ठतः सदा / समस्तविषयास्वादो भक्तेष्व् एवास्ति को ऽप्य् अहो

entries.title: The Wonderful Deceiver
entries.en:
namas to the deceptive, the pure, the secret,
the manifest-self, the subtle, the all-form —
to the citra, to śambhu.
entries.brief: Bowing to the wonderful one whose wonder IS his trick.
entries.logic: Citra — variegated, marvellous, strange — is the epithet running through the verse, married to māyāvine (the deceiver), prakaṭātmane (the manifest secret). The universe's strangeness is his craft, not a malfunction. Adbhuta here is delight in the trick: the weirdness of the world is filed as artistry.
entries.howto: When the world turns surreal — say the verse and file the strangeness under citra. Feeling-tip: the uncanny flips from threat to artistry; the trick becomes someone's excellent work.
entries.iast: māyāvine viśuddhāya guhyāya prakaṭātmane / sūkṣmāya viśvarūpāya namaś citrāya śambhave
entries.devanagari: मायाविने विशुद्धाय गुह्याय प्रकटात्मने / सूक्ष्माय विश्वरूपाय नमश् चित्राय शम्भवे

entries.title: The Wheel of Diverse States
entries.iast: ya eṣa vitatasphuradvividhabhāvacakrātmakaḥ parasparavibhedavānviṣayatāmupāgacchati yadekamayabhāvanāvaśata etyabhedānvayaṃ sa śaṃbhuraśivāpaho jayati bodhabhāsāṃ nidhiḥ
entries.en: he who, made of the widely flashing wheel of diverse states, comes to be the objects of experience — whose one, given to contemplation, is the bond of non-difference: he, śaṃbhu, averter of woe, triumphs — treasury of the lights of knowing.
entries.brief: Abhinavagupta's own opening: the wheel of states resolves into one — triumph.
entries.logic: The Gītārthasaṃgraha's first breath performs its thesis: the flash-wheel of manifold states (thoughts, emotions, the day's weather — the very stuff of experience) resolves into abheda, non-difference — and that resolution is jayati, triumph. Adbhuta as the wonder OF the doctrine: the many flashing states are not noise but the treasury-house (nidhi) of knowing-light.
entries.howto: Use it as the invocation before any prayer-session in this book: name the swirl of your current states as the wheel, then remember the wheel IS the treasury. Feeling-tip: the chaos of feelings gets reclassified as treasure on sight.
entries.devanagari: य एष विततस्फुरद्विविधभावचक्रात्मकः परस्परविभेदवान्विषयतामुपागच्छति यदेकमयभावनावशत एत्यभेदान्वयं स शंभुरशिवापहो जयति बोधभासां निधिः

entries.title: Worship Without Begging
entries.en:
wonder! o boon-giver: among the full-hearted in devotion toward you,
is any mode of worship praised
that is not stained with begging?
entries.brief: The great wonder: worship with no shopping list attached.
entries.logic: Vismaya at the bhaktas whose pūjā carries no yācñā — no begging-stain. The worship without a price-tag is the marvel; the wonder is the devotee's purity of motive, not the display. Adbhuta turns inward: amazed at the possibility of asking for nothing.
entries.howto: Notice when you've prayed with a shopping list. Say this verse as the correction, then worship once with nothing attached. Feeling-tip: the ask drops and the song stays — that gap is the wonder.
entries.iast: aho bhaktibharodāracetasāṃ varada tvayi / slāghyaḥ pūjāvidhiḥ ko 'pi yo na yācñākalaṃkitaḥ
entries.devanagari: अहो भक्तिभरोदारचेतसां वरद त्वयि / स्लाघ्यः पूजाविधिः को ऽपि यो न याच्ञाकलंकितः

entries.title: The Rasa Beyond the World
entries.en:
diving in the ocean of devotion's nectar — with peaceful waves,
cool and white and sweet — tasting the alaukika rasa:
who among the steady even counts a name there?
entries.brief: Śānta's theory in one verse: the peaceful ocean, the non-worldly taste.
entries.logic: Everything the Abhinavabhāratī says about rasa is here: śānta-kallola — the peace-wave ocean; svādubhakti-sudhāmbudhi — the nectar-ocean of sweet devotion; and alaukika-rasa-āsvāda — the BEYOND-WORLDLY tasting. Peace is not absence but the most extreme flavour, so intense that the steady (susthā) stop counting even names.
entries.howto: For peace-practice: dive once, taste once, count nothing — not even the breath. Feeling-tip: the mental to-do list stops being readable; that illegibility is the alaukika flicker.
entries.iast: śāntakallolaśītācchasvādubhaktisudhāmbudhau / alaukikarasāsvāde susthaiḥ ko 'nāma gaṇyate
entries.devanagari: शान्तकल्लोलशीताच्छस्वादुभक्तिसुधाम्बुधौ / अलौकिकरसास्वादे सुस्थैः को ऽनाम गण्यते

entries.title: All Time in the Worship-Union
entries.brief: The peaceful life defined: every hour inside the worship-union.
entries.logic: Kāla (time) is the anxious substance — endless time is the dread of the future. The verse re-routes every hour into bhavat-pūjāmaya-saṅga-sukha, the happiness of joining-with-worship. Śānta as temporal peace: not a mood but a schedule filled with one activity. And the craving (īyadarthaye) is permitted — it is the only thirst worth keeping.
entries.howto: When the day stretches ahead daunting: pray the WHOLE day into the worship-frame, then do the next ordinary thing as its first item. Feeling-tip: the horizon softens; time becomes a room, not a corridor.
entries.iast: bhavatpūjāmayāsaṅgasambhogasukhino mama / prayātu kālaḥ sakalo 'py ananto 'pīyadarthaye
entries.devanagari: भवत्पूजामयासङ्गसम्भोगसुखिनो मम / प्रयातु कालः सकलो ऽप्य् अनन्तो ऽपीयदर्थये

entries.title: For Peace, Not for Pleasure
entries.en:
for peace, not for pleasure-seeking — those intoxicated
with the fullness of your devotion, o lord;
even the fruit of searching for liberation they don't crave —
before you, the heart-stealer.
entries.brief: The anti-materialist verse: peace sought as peace, not as payoff.
entries.logic: The devotee's intoxication aims at śāntaye — peace — na sukhalipsutā, explicitly NOT the pleasure-hunt; even mokṣa-phala (the fruit of liberation) is not craved. Śānta is the only desire that cancels desiring — and the verse says so without smugness: these ones don't even want the prize.
entries.howto: When peace turns into another acquisition-plan — this retreat, that technique, the next course — say it as the disarming. Feeling-tip: the goal releases you; the practice continues unburdened.
entries.iast: śāntaye na sukhalipsutā manāg bhaktisambhṛtamadeṣu taiḥ prabhoḥ / mokṣamārgaṇaphalāpi nārthanā smaryate hṛdayahāriṇaḥ puraḥ
entries.devanagari: शान्तये न सुखलिप्सुता मनाग् भक्तिसम्भृतमदेषु तैः प्रभोः / मोक्षमार्गणफलापि नार्थना स्मर्यते हृदयहारिणः पुरः

entries.title: Cries Like Bamboo-Drops
entries.en:
laying my cries at your ear's place, my dearest —
they grow small: like rain inside a bamboo-joint,
they rise as pearls.
entries.brief: Even the cries get smaller when laid at his ear.
entries.logic: The simile IS the practice: ākranda (cries) laid at his ear-shore become tucchatarāṇi — tinier — like rain slipping down inside a hollow bamboo. Śānta as acoustics: devotion is the volume knob. No silencing, no denial — just the difference between shouting into the void and speaking into an ear.
entries.howto: When crying or complaining: say it and consciously LAY the noise at his ear — the listener inside. Feeling-tip: the sound gets smaller mid-sentence; the bamboo-joint is the quiet place behind your own listening.
entries.iast: tvatkarṇadeśama dhiśayya mahārghabhāvam ākranditāni mama tucchatarāṇi yānti / vaṃśāntarālapatitāni jalaikadeśakhaṇḍāni mauktikamaṇitvam ivodvahanti
entries.devanagari: त्वत्कर्णदेशम धिशय्य महार्घभावम् आक्रन्दितानि मम तुच्छतराणि यान्ति / वंशान्तरालपतितानि जलैकदेशखण्डानि मौक्तिकमणित्वम् इवोद्वहन्ति
